# Copilot / AI coding agent instructions — own_yourself

Purpose
- Help contributors edit, build, and extend this Flutter app. Focus on concrete, repository-specific patterns and commands.

Big picture
- This is a single Flutter application (entry: [lib/main.dart](lib/main.dart#L1)).
- Platform-specific folders exist for Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, and web. Native plugin registration is generated (see `ios/Flutter/GeneratedPluginRegistrant.*` and `macos/Flutter/GeneratedPluginRegistrant.swift`).
- Android uses Kotlin Gradle DSL (`android/build.gradle.kts`, `android/app/build.gradle.kts`). The Android Gradle build directory is intentionally remapped to the repo-level `build/` (see [android/build.gradle.kts](android/build.gradle.kts#L1)).

Key files to inspect when making changes
- App entry and UI: [lib/main.dart](lib/main.dart#L1)
- Shared utilities: `lib/utils/` (example: [lib/utils/colors.dart](lib/utils/colors.dart#L1))
- Dependencies and SDK: [pubspec.yaml](pubspec.yaml#L1)
- Android Gradle Kotlin DSL: [android/app/build.gradle.kts](android/app/build.gradle.kts#L1)
- iOS AppDelegate and plugin registration: [ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift](ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift#L1)
- Project linting rules: [analysis_options.yaml](analysis_options.yaml#L1)

Developer workflows (explicit commands)
- Install deps: `flutter pub get`
- Run on a device: `flutter run -d <device-id>` (or `flutter run -d macos` / `-d ios` / `-d chrome`)
- Build artifacts:
  - Android APK: `flutter build apk` (or use `./gradlew` in `android/` for lower-level tasks)
  - iOS: `flutter build ios` then open `ios/Runner.xcworkspace` in Xcode for signing
  - macOS: `flutter build macos`
- Analyze & tests: `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` (no tests currently in repo; add tests under `test/`).

Project-specific conventions and patterns
- Do not edit generated files: `GeneratedPluginRegistrant.*`, files under `ios/Flutter/` or `macos/Flutter/` are generated by Flutter tooling.
- Android uses Kotlin DSL (`.kts`) — keep edits in Kotlin syntax (do not convert to Groovy).
- Colors and simple design tokens are defined as integer constants in `lib/utils/colors.dart`. Use them via `Color(AppColors.primaryColor)` in widgets.
- Linting: `flutter_lints` is configured; follow the style implied by `analysis_options.yaml`.

Integration points & external dependencies
- This project currently has no explicit MethodChannel or manual platform-channel code (search for `MethodChannel` if you intend to add native comms).
- Native plugins are registered via Flutter's generated registrants. When adding plugins, run `flutter pub get` and rebuild to regenerate platform registration.

When updating platform code
- Android: prefer testing with `flutter run -d emulator-xxx` and, for advanced Gradle tasks, use `./gradlew` inside `android/` (Kotlin DSL). Note build dir is remapped to the repo-level `build/`.
- iOS/macOS: open the corresponding workspace in Xcode for signing and developer provisioning checks.

PR guidance for AI agents
- Make minimal, well-scoped changes; update `pubspec.yaml` only when adding dependencies and run `flutter pub get` locally.
- Avoid touching generated files or the remapped build config unless necessary; point reviewers to the exact platform steps for manual verification (e.g., opening Xcode for iOS signing).
- Provide concrete code examples in PR descriptions and reference the key files above.

Examples
- Using the color constant in a widget: `Container(color: Color(AppColors.primaryColor))` — see [lib/utils/colors.dart](lib/utils/colors.dart#L1).

If anything here is unclear or incomplete, ask for the exact file or command to verify and I will update this guidance.
